evidence.description: Task { await restore() } is called inside init without being awaited or managed.

candidates.explanation: The `init` method launches an unawaited `Task` to perform asynchronous work. This can lead to race conditions or unexpected behavior during object initialization, as the object might be used before the initialization work (restoring state) is complete.
candidates.title: Unawaited Task in Initializer

evidence.description: Task { do { ... } catch { ... } } is used to perform network loading and state updates.

candidates.explanation: The `load` method launches an unawaited `Task` that performs network requests and updates state. This makes the method's execution non-deterministic and can lead to multiple concurrent loads overlapping if the method is called rapidly.
candidates.title: Unawaited Task for Network Request

evidence.description: state property performs a sort on the items collection on every access.

candidates.explanation: The `state` computed property performs a sorting operation (`sorted`) every time it is accessed. This can be inefficient if the `items` set is large and the property is accessed frequently.
candidates.title: Inefficient Computed Property

evidence.description: Manual use of Task.detached followed by MainActor.run inside a class already isolated to @MainActor.

candidates.explanation: The `restore` method uses `Task.detached` to perform file I/O and then switches back to `MainActor.run` to update `items`. This is redundant because the class is already marked with `@MainActor`, and the `Task` could be managed more cleanly using the actor's context.
candidates.title: Redundant Actor Switching

candidates.explanation: The `needsUpdate` property accesses `User.shared.news`, which is a global shared state. This can lead to side effects or inconsistent behavior if the shared state is modified by other parts of the application simultaneously.
candidates.title: Dependency on Global Shared State
